The Petitioners have filed this petition against Respondents for the relief of compensation under Sec.166 of Motors Vehicles Act, 1989.

2. After receipt of records from the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.4920/2021 (MV)
dated 09.11.2022, petitioner No.1 is examined further and she exhibited documents marked as Ex.P.21 to Ex.P.25 including bank statement and IT returns.

SCCH 5 R. Varshitha vs Siddappa on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70931685/
2 3.
The brief facts of case is as under:
That on 13.07.2018 at about 9.35 a.m. K.Padma has been riding her Yamaha Cygnus Ray-Z bearing Reg.No.KA-02-JF-7491 opp.

SK Lavanya Textiles, Near BB Junction,
Mysuru road, Bengaluru, at that time, a Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-41-C-1120 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner and dashed against her two wheeler, as a result of which, she fell down and driver of the tipper lorry ran over.
Immediately after the accident, she was taken to Victoria Hospital, but she succumbed to the injuries on the way to the hospital.

4. At the time of accident, deceased was aged about 46 years, working as an Accountant in M/s.
Anjanadri Interiors, thereby drawing Rs.36,000/- p.m.
Petitioner No.1 and 2 are the daughters of the deceased/K. Padma, due to sudden demise of the SCCH 5 deceased, petitioners have lost their bread earner of the family and lost her love and affection.

Out of the said accident, crime No.38/2018 is registered against the driver of the Tipper Lorry Goods bearing Reg.No.KA-41-C- 1120 before the Chickpet Traffic Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is driver, respondent No.2 is owner of the said tipper lorry, respondent No.3 is insurer, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
So that, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.2,50,00,000/- and respondent No.4 is husband of the deceased K.Padma.
5. On service of notice, respondent No.1, 2 and 4 have remained absent, hence placed exparte.

Respondent No.3/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denied issuance of insurance policy to the Tipper SCCH 5 Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-41-C-1120 and if there is any liability, it is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
He is entitled to take shelter under Sec.147 and 149(2) of M.V.Act.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further submitted that, driver of the said tipper lorry was not holding valid and effective driving license and the said vehicle does not possessed valid permit and FC as on the date of accident.
Further denied relationship of the petitioners with the deceased and also denied age, occupation and income of the deceased.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

6. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
SCCH 5 ::ISSUES::
1.

Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased Smt.K.Padma, W/o. S. Rajkumar,
aged about 46 years was died in a road traffic accident that occurred on 13.07.2018 at about 9.35 a.m. while deceased was driving her Yamaha Cygnus Ray Z bearing Reg.No. KA-02-JF-7491 when she came near BB Junction, Opp. Lavanya Textiles on Mysore Road, at that time, a driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.
KA-41-C-1120 driven in rash and negligent manner and dashed against her vehicle, as a result of which she sustained fatal injuries and died, as mentioned in claim R. Varshitha vs Siddappa on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70931685/
3 petition?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation as prayed in the petition? If so, from which respondent?
3. What order or award?

sentences.text: 7. In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 /daughter of the deceased has deposed her evidence as SCCH 5 PW-1, Proprietor of Anjanadri Interiiors by name Yuvaraj is examined as PW-2 and marked 20 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.20 and closed her evidence.

On the other hand,
respondents have not adduced any evidence.
8. After remand from the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, PW-1 has exhibited 5 documents marked as Ex.P.21 to Ex.P.25 and closed her evidence.
9. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record.

Then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
10. Issue No.1:- In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1/daughter of the deceased has deposed SCCH 5 her evidence as PW-1, in her chief-examination she has reiterated the facts narrated in their petition.

In this regard copy of FIR and complaint is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of inquest report is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of P.M. Report is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.7.
11.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and the records those have marked i.e., FIR with complaint,
charge sheet, mahazar, sketch, inquest report, P.M.Report and IMV Report corroborates the case of the petitioners about causing of the accident dated 13.07.2018 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
SCCH 5 12.

Per contra, except appearance and filing written statement, respondent No.3 has not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non- causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioners about death of K.Padma out of the accident held on 13.07.2018 at about 9.35 a.m. while she was riding Yamaha Cygnus Ray-Z bearing Reg.No.KA-02-JF- 7491 R. Varshitha vs Siddappa on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70931685/
4 opposite to SK Lavanya Textiles, near BB Junction, Mysuru Road, Bengaluru.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioners.

13. On the other hand, there is no defence evidence and police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the driver of the Tipper SCCH 5 Lorry carrying bearing Reg.No.KA-41-C-1120.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioners, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioners have proved the above issue No.1 in their favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:-

As per the case of the petitioners, deceased/K.Padma was aged about 46 years as on the date of accident, for proof of age of the deceased, petitioners have furnished copy of driving license marked as Ex.P.13, wherein date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 26.12.1972, the alleged accident was occurred on 13.07.2018.

Accordingly relying on Ex.P.13 driving license of the deceased, age of the deceased is considered about 46 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 13 is applicable with reference to SCCH 5 decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

15. As per the case of the petitioners, deceased was working as an Accountant in Anjanadri Interiors,
thereby drawing salary of Rs.36,000/- p.m.

In this regard, petitioners have produced salary slip marked as Ex.P.8, Degree Certificate of the deceased marked as Ex.P.22, Provisional Degree Certificate of Padma K. marked as Ex.P.22, marks card marked as Ex.P.23, IT Returns for the year 2016-17 and 2017-18 marked as Ex.P.24 and SBI Bank Pass Book marked as Ex.P.25.

16. Further the proprietor of Anjanadri Interiors by name Yuvaraj is examined as PW-2 who got exhibited copy of GST certificate marked as Ex.P.16, attendance certificate marked as Ex.P.17, copy of partnership deed SCCH 5 marked as Ex.P.18, copy of Firm Registration Certificate is marked as Ex.P.19 and notarized copy of ID Card is marked as Ex.P.20.
17.

Further admittedly the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.4920/2021 has confirmed the liability and negligence on the findings given by the predecessor of this court and only for fresh consideration in respect of quantum of the compensation, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has remanded the matter.
18.
After remanding the case, admittedly PW-1 to substantiate her case has exhibited documents as per Ex.P.21 to Ex.P.25.

Ex.P.21 is degree certificate of deceased K.Padma, Ex.P.22 is provisional degree certificate, Ex.P.23 is marks card, Ex.P.24 is IT returns for the year 2016-17 and 2017-18 of deceased and Ex.P.25 is bank passbook.

So on careful perusal of all SCCH 5 these documents including Ex.P.17 i.e., attendance certificate issued by PW-2 corroborates the case of the petitioners that, during the lifetime of deceased K.Padma, she was working in the PW-2 company and as per Ex.P.17 deceased K.Padma was present for work in the company of PW-2.

Further on perusal of Ex.P.21 which is Bachelors of Commerce Certificate, Ex.P.22 is provisional degree certificate further indicates to the court about completion of the degree course by the K.Padma, so that, she is qualified for earnings in the company of PW-2.

sentences.text: Further very significant document in this case is Ex.P.24, as per this document for the year 2016-17 and 2017-18 her income is declared as Rs.3,57,993/- and Rs.3,95,252/-.

So as per the IT returns placed by the PW-1 i.e., Ex.P.24 in the assessment year 2016-17 and 2017-18 deceased K.Padma has filed IT returns to the IT SCCH 5 department and she has declared her income as stated supra.

Ofcourse on perusal of Ex.P.25 bank passbook, only there is an entry of Rs.20,866/-
dated 07.03.2017, Rs.28,614/- and Rs.12,304/- dated 08.03.2017.
Further there is no entry with regard to the salary paid by PW-2 though it is not a sole ground to disbelieve the earnings of the deceased K.Padma during her lifetime.

20. Further to substantiate petitioner's case, they have also examined employer of deceased K.Padma as PW-2 i.e., Yuvaraj, in his evidence he has clearly stated about payment of Rs.36,000/-
p.m. every month to K.Padma for her work i.e., she was an employee in the organisation of PW-2 and deceased Padma was working as an accountant.

So on perusal of overall documents and comparisons between the evidence of PW-1 and PW-2, IT returns marked as Ex.P.24, bank pass book SCCH 5 marked as Ex.P.25 and Ex.P.8 salary slip of deceased K.Padma, this court comes to the conclusion and deceased monthly income is taken into consideration of Rs.33,000/- at the time of her death by considering the IT returns placed by the PW-1, because Smt.K.Padma has filed IT returns to the IT department, in this document itself she has declared her annual income as Rs.3,57,993/- for the assessment year 2016-17 and Rs.3,95,252/- for the assessment year 2017-18.
Accordingly the monthly income of the deceased is taken as Rs.33,000/- p.m. for the purpose of calculation of loss of dependency.
21. Further petitioner No.1 and 2 are daughters of the deceased/K.Padma.

To prove the said facts,
they have furnished notarized copy of aadhar cards marked as Ex.P.11 and 12 which reveals that,
they are legal SCCH 5 representatives of the deceased K.Padma, hence they become the dependents of the deceased.
Respondent No.4 being father of the petitioners has not come forward to lead his evidence to prove the relationship with the petitioners or his dependency on the income of the deceased.

Further he has left the petitioners and deceased K.Padma in the year 2010 and filed M.C.No.2674/2018 seeking divorce, but till today he has not come forward to prove the relationship or his dependency on the petitioners.
Hence, respondent No.4 is not entitled for any compensation.

22. As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the number of dependents are 2 to 3, then 1/3rd of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so that, 1/3rd of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.
SCCH 5 23.

In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi, The Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that, an addition of 25% to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged above 40 years, in case of self employed person or person having fixed salary as future prospects.

In the case on hand, the monthly income of the deceased is taken as Rs.33,000/- hence, which is taken for additional weightage at the rate of 25%
with reference to her age.

sentences.text: Hence, the following calculation is made for loss of dependency.

Sl. Particulars Calculation Total No.
 (i) Monthly Income Rs.33,000/-
(ii) 25% of (i) above if Rs.33,000/- (+) added to the Rs.8,250/- = monthly income as Rs.41,250/-
future prospects SCCH 5 (iii) 1/3rd of (ii) of the Rs.41,250/- (-) same to be deducted Rs.13,750/- = towards personal and living expenses Monthly income Rs.27,500/-

(iv) Compensation after Rs.27,500/- x Rs.42,90,000/-
multiplier of 13 is 12 x 13 applied 25.
Petitioner No.1 and 2 being the daughters of the deceased are entitled for Rs.20,000/- each towards loss of parental consortium.
Further they are entitled for loss of estate of Rs.15,000/- and also they are entitled for funeral expenses for an amount of Rs.15,000/-.

26. The details of compensation awarded is as under:
Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount/Rs.
1. Loss of dependency 42,90,000-00 2. Loss of parental consortium 40,000-00 (Rs.20,000/- each to SCCH 5 Petitioner No.2 and 3)
3. Loss of Estate 15,000-00 4.
Funeral Expenses 15,000-00 Total 43,60,000-00 27.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.43,60,000/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

28. In the case on hand, respondent No.3 being the insurer has issued insurance policy in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-41-C-1120 bearing No.140521823340009388 which is valid from 21.06.2018 to 20.06.2019, the alleged accident was occurred on 13.07.2018 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of R2 shall go against R3, SCCH 5 so that, R3/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.

R. Varshitha vs Siddappa on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70931685/
7
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
29. Issue No.3:

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.43,60,000/- (Rupees Forty Three Lakhs Sixty Thousand Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.3 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
SCCH 5 The Petitioners are entitled for compensation at the ratio 50:50 in the award amount.
The petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to their accounts on furnishing the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on the computer, typed by her, thereof is corrected and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 1st day of October, 2024)
(MANJUNATHA K.P.) VIII ADDL. JUDGE & COURT OF SMALL CAUSES & ACJM, BENGALURU.
